purpose: Independent practice of A6.12 — listening to (or reading) a story, choosing the operation, modelling with cubes or coins, and writing the equation.
student_learning_goal: I can listen to a snack-shop story, act it out with cubes, and tell how many are altogether or how many are left.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can listen to a snack-shop story, act it out with cubes, and tell how many are altogether or how many are left.
header.character_watermark: Penny the Lead Coin Counter in the top-right corner of the header, holding a tray of cookies. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Read each story. Decide if you ADD or TAKE AWAY. Write the operation and the answer.
parts.visual_layout: Top third of the page. Three numbered rows. Each row has a small illustration on the left (~1.2in tall), a 1–2 sentence story in the middle, and a blank equation line on the right. Story 1 (add): pennies; Story 2 (take away): cookies; Story 3 (add): popcorn. Each illustration features Penny or Nick at the snack shop.

image_placeholders.description: Three small B&W line-art scenes, each ~1.2in tall, stacked vertically. Scene 1: Penny holds a small pile of pennies, with 3 more pennies sliding down toward her hand (add story). Scene 2: A cookie tray with 8 cookies, 2 with bites taken (take away story). Scene 3: Nick adds a bag of popcorn to a small pile (add story). Each scene has a thought-bubble or motion-line cue indicating direction (more in vs going away).
image_placeholders.placement: Top third of the page, three scenes stacked vertically with stories beside.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P1_THREE_STORY_SCENES at top third: keywords (snack, pennies, cookies, popcorn) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Story 1 (Penny had 6 pennies. A customer gave her 3 more): 6 + 3 = 9. Story 2 (Penny baked 8 cookies; 2 got nibbled): 8 − 2 = 6. Story 3 (Nick had 4 bags of popcorn; he made 5 more): 4 + 5 = 9.

parts.student_instructions: Read the story. Draw what happens in three boxes: the START, the CHANGE, and the END. Then write the equation.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two stacked story rows. Each row has a story sentence at the top and three labelled boxes below: START | CHANGE | END. Each box is ~1.5in × 1.2in with light-grey outlines for drawing. Story A: 'Penny had 4 cubes; Nick gave her 3 more.' Story B: 'Quincy had 9 pennies; Nick took 5.' Below each row, a blank equation line.

image_placeholders.description: Two stacked story-modelling rows in B&W line-art. Each row has three labelled boxes side-by-side: START | CHANGE | END. Each box ~1.5in × 1.2in with solid grey outlines for drawing. Above each row, the story sentence is printed in a banner. Below each row, a faint dotted line for the equation.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; two rows spanning full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P2_START_CHANGE_END_BOXES at middle: keywords (story, start, change, end) name what the boxes show.

parts.answer_key: Story A: START 4 cubes, CHANGE +3 cubes (drawn or arrowed in), END 7 cubes; equation 4 + 3 = 7. Story B: START 9 pennies, CHANGE −5 pennies (crossed out or arrowed away), END 4 pennies; equation 9 − 5 = 4.

parts.student_instructions: Look at the equation 6 − 2 = 4. Write your OWN snack-shop story that matches. Use the sentence starters to help.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A target equation banner at the top reads '6 − 2 = 4' in large print. Below that, four sentence-starter lines: '___ had 6 ___.', '___ took (or gave away) 2.', 'Now there are 4 ___.', and 'I used: ADD / TAKE AWAY' (circle one). To the right, a blank box for an optional drawing of the story.

image_placeholders.description: A horizontal banner at the top of Part 3 in B&W line-art. The banner shows the equation '6 − 2 = 4' in large bold numerals (~3in tall). Decorative cookies and pennies frame the equation. To the right of the banner, a blank drawing box (~2in × 2in) with a light-grey outline for the child's optional illustration.
image_placeholders.placement: Bottom of the page, banner spanning full width with optional drawing box on the right.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P3_STORY_BUILDER_BANNER at bottom: keywords (equation, story, snack) name what the banner shows.

parts.answer_key: Any plausible take-away story to 6 − 2 = 4. Examples: 'Penny had 6 cookies. Nick took 2. Now there are 4 cookies.' 'Quincy had 6 pennies. Penny used 2 for the snack shop. Now there are 4 pennies left.' Accept any story where (a) the start is 6, (b) something is taken away or used, (c) 4 are left, and (d) the child circles TAKE AWAY.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and write a story for the equation 5 + 2 = 7! Use the snack shop too.
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation; this is the keystone worksheet because A6.12 lives or dies on operation choice. Hand out at the end of the small-group rotation. Watch for: (a) right answer with wrong operation symbol — diagnostic for the lesson 3 expanded_walkthrough recovery moves; (b) a child who writes the wrong story for Part 3 (e.g. an add story to a take-away equation) — flag for re-loop on the keyword chart. Use Part 2 as evidence for the formative tracker.
